clock.title: The post-election clock in Basic Law: The Government

rows.label: 1. Consultations and first mandate
cells: The president, after consulting every list entering the Knesset
Within 7 days of the official results (art. 7)

rows.label: 2. First attempt
cells: The Knesset member given the task
28 days, plus up to 14 more at the president's discretion (art. 8)

rows.label: 3. Second mandate
cells: The president picks another member, or tells the Speaker there is no prospect
Within 3 days; the second candidate has 28 days, no extension (art. 9)

rows.label: 4. The Knesset's turn
cells: A majority of Knesset members (61) may ask, in writing, for a named member
Request within 21 days; the president assigns the task within 2 days, and that member then has 14 days (art. 10)

rows.label: 5. Dissolution
cells: Automatic if no request is made or the third attempt fails
New election on the last Tuesday before 90 days have passed (art. 11)

rows.label: 6. Confidence vote
cells: The Knesset, after the government presents its guidelines and ministers
A sitting within 7 days of the Knesset being notified (art. 13)

clock.question: Time limits for forming a government after an election, as set in articles 7–13.
clock.source: Basic Law: The Government, Knesset unofficial English translation (amendments through Aug 15, 2023)
clock.note: Different steps apply when a government falls mid-term (a no-confidence vote, art. 28, or a prime minister's dissolution order, art. 29).

five-elections.title: Five elections, 2019–2022: what followed each

rows.label: April 9, 2019
cells: Netanyahu could not form a coalition in the 42 days allowed; the Knesset voted 74–45 to dissolve itself (May 30)
None

rows.label: September 17, 2019
cells: Netanyahu, then Gantz, failed; no candidate gathered 61 signatures in the 21-day window, and the Knesset dissolved (Dec 11)
None

rows.label: March 2, 2020
cells: Netanyahu–Gantz rotation government; the Knesset dissolved in December 2020 when the budget was not passed
May 17, 2020, by 73–46 (76 days after the vote)

rows.label: March 23, 2021
cells: Eight-party Bennett–Lapid government; the Knesset dissolved itself 92–0 on June 30, 2022

rows.label: November 1, 2022
cells: Netanyahu, recommended by 64 members, formed a six-party coalition; the Knesset served until July 2026

five-elections.note: Each row cites its own Times of Israel report. Day counts are the days from election day to the swearing-in, computed from those dates. The December 2020 dissolution: IDI, Jan 28, 2026. Gantz's 2019 mandate: Times of Israel, Oct 23, 2019. The 2022 recommendations: Al Jazeera, Nov 11, 2022. Coalition parties: IDI, Apr 15, 2026. The 25th Knesset's dissolution: Ynet, July 17, 2026.

coalition-size.title: Knesset members in the coalition when each government was formed, 1992–2022
coalition-size.question: MKs in the coalition, as of the day the government was sworn in and up to a week afterwards.
coalition-size.note: Out of 120 seats. Elections in April and September 2019 produced no government, so they have no bar.
